args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN OF REORGANIZATION — DEVIATION REPORT
Committee Redline vs. Debtor Original Plan
Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Deliverable: plan-deviation-report.docx
Classification: Attorney Work Product — Privileged & Confidential

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This report compares the official committee of unsecured creditors' redlined Plan of Reorganization (the "Committee Markup" or "Redline") against the debtor's original proposed Plan of Reorganization (the "Debtor Plan" or "Base Plan"), reconciling the Redline against (i) the valuation summary referenced in the deal materials, (ii) the controlling deal-team / partner transmittal instruction, and (iii) the disclosure-statement schedules and exhibits that qualify the Base Plan.

Three material deviations are introduced by the Committee Markup:

  (1) Indemnification economics — silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the loss basket from a deductible (threshold) basket to a tipping (first-dollar once exceeded) basket;
  (2) Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue in this case, intersecting Schedule 3.7 pending regulatory inquiries; and
  (3) Survival / limitation period — a new limitation period that shortens survival for core representations, contradicting the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner email in the deal-correspondence thread): the client will concede the basket conversion, but any reduction of the survival period is a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and must not drive the recommendation.

Recommendation posture (summary):
  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): ACCEPT / CONCEDE per controlling instruction.
  • Silent indemnification-cap reduction: REJECT or require express, quantified negotiation tied to valuation and Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation; do not accept "silent" economics.
  • MAE regulatory carve-outs: REJECT or narrowly counter; Schedule 3.7 makes the carve-out case-specific and value-shifting.
  • Survival-period shortening: REJECT — walk-away issue under controlling instruction; restore Exhibit B survival matrix.

================================================================================
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED
================================================================================

Primary matter file
  • Deal materials — bankruptcy-restructuring analyze: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization (Matter File 4) — engagement instruction to compare committee redline to debtor original plan using valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts.

Counterparty / committee markup
  • Counterparty markup — bankruptcy-restructuring (committee revision of plan terms). States that most firm-standard / Base Plan provisions are accepted, but identifies the three deviation categories listed above and requires reconciliation against base bankruptcy-restructuring materials before drafting.

Schedules and exhibits (disclosure-statement excerpts / qualifying schedules)
  • Schedule 3.7 — discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE regulatory carve-outs.
  • Schedule 5.2 — lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift.
  • Exhibit B — sets the survival matrix that the markup's limitation-period change contradicts.
  • Governing principle stated in the schedules file: scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base bankruptcy-restructuring materials.

Deal correspondence (transmittal / priority instruction)
  • Partner email thread. Latest message revises analysis priorities: client concedes basket conversion; treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Only the latest message controls; earlier opposite priority ordering is superseded.

Excluded
  • Unrelated administrative correspondence (misfiled distractor) — not relied upon.

Note on valuation summary
  • The engagement instruction requires use of the attached valuation summary. No standalone numerical valuation exhibit beyond the economic implications embedded in the indemnification / retained-liability / survival framework was separately populated in the matter corpus. Economic impact is therefore analyzed qualitatively by reference to (a) silent cap reduction, (b) tipping-basket first-dollar exposure once the basket is exceeded, and (c) Schedule 5.2 retained-liability shift, each of which alters creditor recoveries and residual estate value relative to the Debtor Plan's disclosed economics. Any final confirmation-hearing valuation bridge should be updated once the quantitative valuation summary figures are confirmed with the financial advisor.

================================================================================
III. METHODOLOGY
================================================================================

1. Treat the Debtor Plan (as qualified by Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B) as the baseline.
2. Isolate each Committee Markup deviation from the counterparty-markup record.
3. Reconcile each deviation against the schedules/exhibits (which control over general base-plan statements).
4. Apply the controlling (latest) partner instruction to accept/reject/counter posture.
5. Flag confirmation, disclosure, and absolute-priority / best-interests implications under 11 U.S.C. §§ 1123, 1125, 1129 where the deviation changes treatment, risk allocation, or disclosed economics.

================================================================================
IV. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Debtor Plan (baseline)
  • Firm-standard / Base Plan indemnification construct: stated cap; deductible (threshold) basket — losses below the basket are borne by the indemnified party and do not count toward recovery until the threshold is cleared; above-threshold losses recoverable only to the excess over the basket (classic deductible structure).
  • Schedule 5.2 enumerates retained liabilities. Under the baseline, those retained items remain allocated as disclosed; indemnification economics are not a back-door reallocation vehicle.

B. Committee Redline
  • Indemnification cap is silently reduced (no conspicuous call-out of the new number or percentage in the markup narrative — economics change without transparent redline commentary proportional to the value shift).
  • Basket converted from deductible to tipping basket: once the basket is exceeded, recovery is from the first dollar of covered losses, not merely the excess over the basket.

C. Schedule / disclosure reconciliation
  • Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities: the cap cut plus tipping mechanics would silently shift economic responsibility for scheduled retained items — increasing effective exposure of the indemnifying constituency and/or depleting value otherwise available to other stakeholders under the Debtor Plan's distribution waterfall.
  • Because scheduled exceptions control over general base statements, any plan or confirmation finding that "indemnification is consistent with the disclosure statement" is false unless the disclosure statement and valuation summary are amended to reflect the new cap, tipping rule, and Schedule 5.2 interaction.

D. Valuation / estate-economics impact
  • Silent cap reduction: directly reduces the backstop available for covered claims; understates risk in any recovery model that assumed the Base Plan cap.
  • Tipping basket: increases expected indemnity outflow relative to a deductible basket of the same nominal size (first-dollar coverage after breach of the threshold), raising the expected drain on the indemnifying source of value (reorganized equity, escrow, note, or estate reserve).
  • Combined with Schedule 5.2, the Redline can re-price retained-liability risk without a corresponding adjustment to class recoveries, feasibility projections, or the liquidation analysis — a disclosure and § 1129(a)(7)/(a)(11) concern if not corrected.

E. Controlling instruction / recommended posture
  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): CONCEDE / ACCEPT per latest partner instruction.
  • Silent cap reduction: DO NOT ACCEPT as a silent change. Require (i) express numeric cap in the plan and disclosure statement, (ii) blackline visibility, (iii) updated valuation / recovery exhibit, and (iv) express statement whether Schedule 5.2 items are in or out of the reduced cap. Counter: restore Base Plan cap, or accept a reduced cap only with quantified consideration (e.g., incremental recovery to the conceding class, escrow sizing, or narrowed indemnity scope).

F. Drafting / disclosure follow-ups if any piece is accepted
  • Amend indemnification section and related definitions.
  • Conform disclosure statement, valuation summary bridge, and any plan supplement escrow/reserve exhibit.
  • Add Schedule 5.2 cross-reference clarifying retained-liability treatment under the new basket and cap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — MAE Definition: Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Debtor Plan (baseline)
  • Standard MAE definition without the committee's new regulatory-action carve-outs of the kind at issue in this matter.
  • Conditionality, termination, bring-down, and related plan/transaction triggers keyed to MAE remain intact as drafted in the Base Plan.

B. Committee Redline
  • MAE definition adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter — i.e., the carve-out is not a generic market-standard regulatory exclusion; it is tailored to neutralize the pending risk profile.

C. Schedule / disclosure reconciliation
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs. The schedules file expressly flags that intersection.
  • Effect: events or developments arising from the Schedule 3.7 inquiries could be excluded from MAE, preventing MAE-based protections (walk rights, bring-down failures, funding conditions, or related plan triggers) that the Debtor Plan would otherwise preserve.
  • Scheduled exceptions control: the existence of Schedule 3.7 means the carve-out is not hypothetical; it is a live allocation of known risk.

D. Valuation / estate-economics impact
  • Shifts regulatory downside from the party that would bear MAE consequences under the Base Plan to the estate / opposing constituencies.
  • May impair feasibility and creditor-recovery assumptions if regulatory outcomes associated with the two inquiries can no longer support MAE remedies or renegotiation leverage.
  • Disclosure statement must describe the carve-out and its interaction with Schedule 3.7; failure to do so risks inadequate information under § 1125.

E. Controlling instruction / recommended posture
  • Partner instruction does not authorize concession on MAE. REJECT the broad regulatory carve-out as drafted.
  • Counter options (in ascending aggressiveness toward committee):
      (1) Delete the new regulatory carve-outs entirely and restore Base Plan MAE;
      (2) Permit only ordinary-course, industry-wide regulatory changes, expressly excluding company-specific actions, the Schedule 3.7 inquiries, and any expansion, adverse finding, fine, or operational restriction arising therefrom;
      (3) If any carve-out remains, require a separate regulatory indemnity, reserve, or escrow sized to the Schedule 3.7 matters, with disclosure-statement risk factors updated accordingly.

F. Drafting / disclosure follow-ups
  • MAE definition and all cross-references (conditions, termination, representations bring-down).
  • Disclosure-statement risk factors and Schedule 3.7 narrative.
  • Any plan findings regarding absence of MAE at confirmation/effective date.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — Survival / Limitation Period Shortening (Core Representations)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Debtor Plan (baseline)
  • Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for core representations (and related claim periods). That matrix is the controlling temporal allocation under the base materials; scheduled/exhibit terms control over general statements.

B. Committee Redline
  • New limitation period shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

C. Schedule / disclosure reconciliation
  • Direct conflict with Exhibit B survival matrix. Under the schedules/exhibits governing rule, Exhibit B controls over a general limitation-period insert in the Redline unless Exhibit B is formally amended through the same disclosure process.
  • Shortened survival reduces the window for indemnity or other remedies tied to core reps — compounding Deviation 1 (weaker indemnification economics) and Deviation 2 (narrower MAE) by also cutting time.

D. Valuation / estate-economics impact
  • Truncated survival reduces expected value of representation-based protections and can recharacterize risk as unrecoverable post-effective-date leakage.
  • Interacts with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities: claims that would have been timely under Exhibit B may fall outside the shortened period, effectively converting contingent indemnity into stranded loss.

E. Controlling instruction / recommended posture
  • WALK-AWAY ISSUE per latest partner instruction. REJECT any survival-period reduction.
  • Required counter: restore Exhibit B survival matrix in full; delete the Redline's shortened limitation period for core representations. No partial days-count compromise without new client authority superseding the walk-away directive.
  • Do not trade survival shortening for the already-conceded basket conversion — the controlling email treats these as asymmetrically prioritized (basket may be given; survival may not).

F. Drafting / disclosure follow-ups if Base Plan survival is restored (expected path)
  • Conform plan survival section to Exhibit B; state that Exhibit B controls in the event of conflict.
  • Disclosure statement must continue to describe the Exhibit B periods; remove any Redline language implying a shorter core-rep survival.

================================================================================
V. CROSS-CUTTING CONFIRMATION AND DISCLOSURE ISSUES
